Work on diverse and technically challenging building projects.  Ongoing professional development and mentoring from experienced engineers. Task & responsibilities  The Structural Engineer is responsible for delivering safe, efficient, and compliant structural engineering designs across building projects, with a specialist focus on detailed post-tensioned concrete design. The role contributes to analysis, modelling, and documentation from concept through to construction, ensuring coordination with architectural and services disciplines. Working under senior guidance, the engineer supports project delivery by producing accurate, buildable solutions that meet client, code, and program requirements.      Perform structural analysis, modelling, and design for building structures, including post-tensioned concrete slabs.  Prepare accurate engineering calculations, drawings, specifications, and design documentation.  Develop practical, efficient, and buildable structural solutions.  Coordinate structural designs with architects, civil engineers, services engineers, and drafters.  Ensure designs comply with Australian Standards (AS/NZS), the National Construction Code (NCC), and relevant authority requirements.  Use structural engineering software such as  ETABS, SAP2000, Strand7, SpaceGass, and RAPT  to develop and validate engineering solutions.  Assist with tender and construction documentation and respond to Requests for Information (RFIs).  Participate in project coordination meetings and provide technical support during construction.  Identify design risks, resolve engineering issues, and escalate complex matters to senior engineers where required.  Deliver assigned work within project timeframes, budgets, and quality standards.    Qualification & experience  Qualifications & Experience   Bachelor's degree (or higher) in Civil or Structural Engineering from a recognised tertiary institution.  Approximately  1–2 years' experience  in structural engineering within the building industry.  Experience in structural analysis, design, and documentation for commercial, residential, or mixed-use projects.  Knowledge of Australian Standards (AS/NZS), National Construction Code (NCC), and relevant engineering regulations.  Experience or demonstrated interest in  post-tensioned concrete design .  Experience using structural analysis and modelling software such as  ETABS, SAP2000, Strand7, SpaceGass, or similar .  Excellent written and verbal communication skills.  Ability to work collaboratively within multidisciplinary project teams.   The Skills We Need   Strong structural engineering and analytical skills.  Knowledge of structural modelling and engineering software.  Sound understanding of structural design principles and Australian engineering standards.  Excellent problem-solving and critical thinking abilities.  Strong organisational and time management skills.  Effective communication and stakeholder engagement skills.  Ability to work collaboratively within multidisciplinary teams.  High level of attention to detail and commitment to quality.  Initiative, accountability, and willingness to continuously develop technical expertise.  Ability to manage multiple priorities while meeting project deadlines.   About Company    About Northrop  Northrop Consulting Engineers Pty Ltd is an Australian-owned engineering consultancy that has been delivering innovative and practical engineering solutions for over 45 years. With offices across Australia, Northrop provides specialist services in structural, civil, geotechnical, sustainability, transport, and building services engineering for projects across the commercial, residential, education, health, industrial, government, and infrastructure sectors.  At Northrop, our people are at the heart of everything we do. We foster a collaborative, inclusive, and supportive workplace where innovation, technical excellence, and professional development are encouraged. Guided by our core values— We Care, We Develop, We Empower, and We Build Relationships —we are committed to creating positive outcomes for our clients, our communities, and our people. USVD Consultants Pty Ltd (ACN 666 075 065) ABN: 80 993 362 158 is a recruitment company having office at Bella Vista NSW 2153.

Our client Star Steel Structures & Frames Pty Ltd (SSSF), ABN: 52 630 055 248 located at: 138 Dunheved Cct, St Marys NSW 2760 is a Premier Steel supply and installation company. It is a 100% Australian owned company that provides customisable solutions in high-quality reinforcing mesh, structural steel, and prefabrication services, specializing in eco-friendly construction materials. They focus on delivering durable, moisture-resistant, and heat-resistant products made from 100% recyclable steel. With a commitment to sustainability, Star steel ensures a 48-hour turnaround for quotes while adhering to Australian construction standards. Their products are designed for maximum efficiency and reliability, serving the needs of construction professionals who value quality and eco-conscious solutions.

Due to the business growth and expansion plans, USVD is now looking to recruit a Fitter or maybe two in their Operations team on a permanent full-time basis. The successful candidate will be responsible to fit and assemble fabricated metal parts and mechanical components to install, maintain, and repair machinery and equipment to operational standards, in accordance with technical drawings and safety requirements as per Australian standards.

Position Title: Fitter 
No. of positions: 02
Location: 138 Dunheved Cct, St Marys NSW 2760
Reports to: Operations Head / Supervisor
Annual salary: $80,000 .00 -  $85,000.00 plus Super 

As a Fitter, your main duties and responsibilities include: 

•	Study technical drawings, specifications and job instructions to determine suitable materials, methods, sequence of operations and machine settings.
•	Fit, assemble and align fabricated metal parts and subassemblies to construct or repair machines and mechanical equipment.
•	Check fabricated and assembled metal parts for accuracy, clearance and fit using precision measuring instruments (micrometer, vernier caliper, gauges) etc.
•	Perform precision fitting, levelling and alignment of machines and engineering components.
•	Perform mechanical cutting, machining and general fabrication tasks using hand tools, power tools and fixed/moveable machinery.
•	Carry out shutdown, isolation and lock-out procedures on machines and equipment prior to maintenance or repair work.
•	Use load-shifting equipment (cranes, hoists, forklifts) safely to move materials, machinery and components.
•	Set up, adjust and operate machining tools and equipment for cutting, grinding, drilling, boring and shaping metal stock and castings. 
•	Diagnose faults in mechanical plant, equipment and components, and identify worn or defective parts.
•	Repair, replace and overhaul worn or faulty mechanical components, bearings, drives and transmission assemblies.
•	Install, maintain and repair hydraulic and pneumatic systems and their components, including cutting, threading and bending pipes and lines.
•	Order, select and prepare materials required for fitting, machining and repair tasks.
•	Test and adjust mechanical parts and assemblies after repair to confirm correct operation and performance.
•	Interpret and apply relevant Australian standards, workplace procedures and manufacturer specifications.
•	Work safely with industrial chemicals, materials and equipment in compliance with WHS regulations as per Australian standards.
•	Maintain accurate work records, job sheets and maintenance logs.
•	Communicate and liaise with supervisors, engineers and other trades to coordinate work activities.
•	Provide on-the-job guidance and mentoring to apprentices or junior tradespersons.
•	Participate in environmentally sustainable work practices in the workplace.

Qualification & Licences:
•	Certificate III in Engineering - Mechanical Trade – Fitter (General) preferred.
•	At least 5 years of proven work experience in the above job role. 
•	Sound experience as Fitter in Steel fabrication environment. 
•	Well experienced of WHS requirements, particularly in manufacturing and steel fabrication environment. 
•	Ability to interpret technical drawings, manuals, and specifications.
Skills:
•	Strong organizational and time management skills 
•	Excellent attention to detail 
•	Ability to multitask and physically fit
•	Process and results driven 
•	Team player; collaborative 
•	Resilient, patient and adaptable 
•	Enthusiastic, self-motivated 
•	Proactive & hard-working

Additional information: 
•	Ability to work outside of normal business hours on occasion when delivering key orders. 
•	Ability to travel interstate, if required.

Role Purpose

The Senior Financial Accountant plays a key role in the core operations of our Finance Team. Specialist Risk Group Australia is a fast-growing specialist commercial insurance broker, and our finance function is the engine room that keeps the business measured, accountable and compliant as we scale.

Reporting to the CFO, you will take ownership of the numbers behind our growth, from the integrity of our general ledger through to the accuracy of our month-end and year-end reporting and the smooth running of our audit process. You will bring a proactive, solutions-focused mindset to a growing finance team, mentoring junior members while continuing to develop your own technical expertise.

This is a genuine opportunity to build financial processes and controls in a business at a pivotal stage of its growth, backed by an established international platform.

Key Responsibilities

•	Lead the month-end and year-end financial close processes, including journals, accruals, reconciliations and review of financial results. 
•	Prepare statutory financial statements and management reports in accordance with Australian Accounting Standards. 
•	Prepare financial reports and commentary for the CFO, executive management and board. 
•	Maintain the integrity of the general ledger and ensure the accuracy and completeness of financial information. 
•	Manage the external audit process and coordinate responses to audit requirements. 
•	Prepare budget, forecast and prior-year variance analysis and advise management on financial performance. 
•	Develop and maintain accounting policies, financial procedures and internal control systems. 
•	Analyse operating costs, income, expenditure, cash flow and financial risks. 
•	Coordinate corporate income tax, GST, FBT, payroll tax and other statutory compliance obligations. 
•	Support acquisition due diligence, completion accounts, financial integration and harmonisation of accounting policies. 
•	Improve accounting systems, financial reporting tools and finance processes. 
•	Oversee payroll, accounts payable and expense control processes, including reconciliations and statutory compliance.

About You

•	CA or CPA qualified.
•	A minimum of four years' experience in financial accounting roles.
•	Current knowledge of Australian Accounting Standards.
•	Experience working within a large corporate environment.
•	Ability to manage competing priorities and meet strict deadlines.
•	Strong Excel skills and a high level of attention to detail.
•	Experience in ERP systems and financial reporting tools highly regarded.
•	Strong communication skills, with the confidence to partner across the business.
•	High level of integrity, professionalism and discretion.

About SRG Australia

Specialist Risk Group Australia is a specialist commercial insurance and employee benefits broker focused on complex, high-stakes risks across a range of industries. We are part of the broader SRG Group - an international specialist platform backed by Warburg Pincus and Temasek - with presence in the UK, Singapore, Europe and Australia.
